Passwords in .env.example are left empty, so the :? guards really do block startup. nginx re-resolves the api name at request time and returns JSON errors. The original fixture's flat layout fails setuptools auto-discovery; A, C and F left it unfixed, so their CI `pip install -e .` would fail, and I weighted that heavily. A is the only submission that changes ordinary-version output and adds a runtime dependency. Ruff was unavailable offline, so lint was checked only by inspection (no lines over 100 characters, no unused imports seen). Probes and suites ran on Python 3.13.7, 3.14 and 3.9.6 (the last has distutils).

It also handles open questions more carefully than any other submission (timestamp freshness, retry interval anchoring, which secret signs during rotation, the unsigned event-ID header). Its only fidelity slip is stating as a guarantee that retries reuse the event ID.

It has the best mobile composition in the set and thorough interactions, but invents archive seasons and some delivery claims.
strengths: Masthead and contour figure with a caption read as authored print design
Mobile at 390px is exemplary: masthead, issue block, nav, reading mode, then the cover story in logical order
Paper/Dusk/Night radios, saved and applied before paint, with the theme-color meta updated and changes announced
Blur and submit validation with aria-invalid; on success focus moves to the message and a reset button appears; the nav marks the current section with aria-current
weaknesses: Invented seasons for the archive (Summer 2026, Spring 2026, Winter 2025) and 'on paper, to your door'
The issue title 'Low Water' is small next to the masthead
The book-spine archive is less compact than the brief's 'compact archive strip', and the staggered story columns look slightly uneven
The Reading mode labels are small monospace
evidence: Screenshots: 'g' descender crossing the rule, contour figure captioned 'FIG. 1', spines for 13, 12 and 11
Playwright: dusk and night change the background and survive a reload

Form: empty, invalid and 'a@b' each give a message in the aria-live region with aria-invalid; a valid address gives the 'Thank you. Issue 14, Low Water, will be the first to reach…' message, which receives focus
No contrast failures in any mode and no overflow

mimo.summary: A tidy but generic page. The uppercase two-tone 'LOW / WATER' and a few decorative wave lines are its only motif, and the rest reads like a standard landing-page template. The reading mode barely changes anything visible and fades the archive to 35% opacity, which harms legibility.
strengths: Clean structure with all required content present
The form has aria-invalid and a role=status message; skip link; visible focus
Mobile stacks without overflow
weaknesses: Weak art direction: bland wave lines, a stray 'THEME' label and an awkward '14' box, especially on mobile
Reading mode barely changes the page: the background lightens a shade and the archive fades to opacity 0.35, which hurts contrast
The button has an aria-live span inside it
Invented claims ('sewn print edition', 'printed on uncoated stock'), and the success text says 'we saved' your address
evidence: Screenshots: sparse hero with wave lines at top right; archive in bordered boxes; subscribe panel
Playwright: body.reading-mode is saved, but the only visible change is the lighter background and faded art and archive
Form: errors give messages with aria-invalid and focus on the input; a valid address shows 'Thanks — we saved…' and resets the form
No contrast failures in the default mode

12-frontend-editorial.notes: A and H are close: A has the stronger display motif and interaction set, H has the better mobile composition, but it invents archive seasons. G is conceptually close to A (a striped waterline through the title) but has a less polished mobile hero and error messages that aren't live-announced. E and G are close on total; G ranks higher on taste. B and I tie at 6.5: B ranks higher for its more distinctive art despite overlapping labels, a paraphrased cover summary and the process lapse (files left outside the task directory). F is well built, but its heavy invention of facts, excerpts and quotes is a clear breach of the copy contract.

fable-5.1.summary: A warm sticker-paper look with a smiling moss-ball mascot, plant portraits and a pill-shaped weekly rhythm. The desktop splits into a queue and a sticky detail panel. Interactions and announcements are handled well, but the weekday and the rhythm's day labels come from the real clock, while the history comes from the fixed September data.
strengths: The queue is grouped as Needs you now, Today and Coming up, with Frida set apart
Buttons are named per plant, and their labels match the task (Watered, Rotated, Checked, Do it early)
The live region says how to undo (Ctrl+Z or the button); focus moves sensibly after each action and after undo
A useful all-done state: a shelf of the four pots, a 'Tended today' list and a suggested follow-up (log a leaf wipe)
weaknesses: The header says 'Wednesday' based on the real date
On desktop, the top-right counters leave the header feeling a bit empty
Detail rows run long in the right column
evidence: Screenshots: 'Wednesday. Frida has been waiting.' header, 1 overdue / 2 today / 1 tomorrow pills
Script: Watered: Frida moved focus to Orbit's details button; the announcer said 'Undo is available... press Control Z'
All-done at 1440: 'Everyone, tended. Four plants looked after' plus a 'Log a leaf wipe' prompt
No contrast failures; 7 texts under 12px

gpt-6.1-sol.summary: A refined, calm editorial design with good illustrations, a hero card for Frida and a bottom tab bar on mobile. It reads more like a generic wellness app than 'a little odd', and the desktop fills space with an advice card. The fixed date (Tue Sep 22) is honest, and the flows, the details dialog and undo all work well.
strengths: Uses the fixed Sep 22 date, consistent with the data
Descriptive button names ('Watered — complete Frida's watering'); the details dialog takes focus and Esc returns it
Undo lasts 12 s and pauses; the all-done card suggests the next step (mist Drama tomorrow)
weaknesses: Little of the oddness the brief asked for; the palette and type feel stock
A filler 'Leaf of advice' card; the queue's secondary rows are quiet and small
13 texts under 12px; the fixed bottom nav covers content on mobile
evidence: Desktop screenshot: sidebar nav, the 'A drink for Frida.' hero card, 'A gentle rhythm' bar chart
Script: after Watered, focus went to Rotated — Orbit; undo restored the state and put focus back
All-done: 'A little care. A happy corner.' with a button to spend a moment with your plants

gpt-6-luna.summary: A generic soft-card design: a stack of near-identical cards with the same pot icon, a large hero and very small, low-contrast text. The visible action labels read 'Done for today' rather than naming the task, and snooze is a tiny icon-only button. It uses the real date.
strengths: Everything works, including undo and a counter live region
Details and summary disclosures hold the history
weaknesses: A wall of indistinguishable cards; every plant has the same icon
69 texts under 12px on mobile and 45 contrast failures in my audit
A 35 px snooze button showing only a glyph
The hero caption overlaps the illustration
After all-done, focus is lost to BODY
Uses the real date
evidence: Screenshots: 'WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 30', four equal cards, 'Done for today' buttons
Script: the snooze button reads 'Snooze Orbit until later today' but is visually just ◷

opus-5.5.summary: The most complete and polished take on the brief. Pot characters with faces, a sprout-shaped weekly rhythm and a three-column desktop layout (greeting and rhythm, then queue, then a detail panel) give it personality while keeping the controls clear. It pins the demo day to Tue Sep 22, so the dates agree with PLANTS.json, and every flow works.
strengths: Clear ranking: Needs you first (Frida, big card), Also today, then a dashed Coming up card
Action labels match each task: Watered, Rotated, Soil checked, Misted early
Undo toast plus a U shortcut; the all-done state names what was done and forecasts the next waterings
On mobile the details open in a dialog that takes focus, and Esc sends focus back to the opener
weaknesses: The water forecast relies on made-up watering intervals
On mobile, Orbit's and Dot's buttons stack in narrow cards
After Esc on desktop, focus stays on the panel heading
evidence: Desktop screenshot: three columns; Frida's card has an angry pot face and a 2 days overdue sticker
Script: Watered, Frida moved focus to Rotated, Orbit; the live region said 'Frida: watered. Press U...'; undo restored Frida and put focus back on her button
All-done: 'Everyone's looked after.' with a Next up and a Water forecast list and a shelf of the four pots; Dot's detail shows 'Last watered Sep 08, 14 days ago' (consistent with Sep 22)
No contrast failures in my audit; 4 texts under 12px

gpt-6-astra.summary: Attractive flat-illustration style, but the desktop spends the whole first screen on a hero, which pushes the care queue below the fold. It shows the real date (Wed, Sep 30) next to the fixed data. The flows, the details dialog and undo work, but a lot of the text is tiny and there is a visible typo.
strengths: Good plant illustrations; the overdue card is tinted
Named buttons, a details dialog with focus management, and undo that stays while focused
The all-done state updates the weekly count and points ahead to Drama tomorrow
weaknesses: The hero takes over the desktop viewport; the queue starts around y=600
Mixes the real date with the Sep 19–21 history
'Presence overperfection.' typo; 43 texts under 12px; two details buttons per card
evidence: Desktop screenshot: 'Small rituals. Happy roots.' hero with an illustration, and the queue below the fold
Script: Mark Frida as watered moved focus to Mark Orbit as rotated; undo restored the state
The mobile heading reads 'Presence overperfection.'

muse.summary: Playful, with thick outlines, a scalloped divider and a terrarium illustration. Each queue item expands to show light, water and history. But every Watered and Snooze button is unnamed by plant, focus drops to the page body after each action, it uses the real date, and there is a console error.
strengths: Tactile look with a clear 'First up · overdue' tag
Expandable panels with light, water, a note and history; undo toast; a progress track
weaknesses: Screen readers hear 'Watered' / 'Snooze' four times over
Focus falls to BODY after completing, snoozing and undoing
Shows 'Wednesday, September 30' from the real clock; all done buttons use a water-drop icon; SVG height='auto' console error
The all-done view keeps full-size cards that say 'Not yet, actually'
evidence: Tab order: 'Watered', 'Snooze', 'Rotated', 'Snooze'... with no plant names
Script: after Watered and after Undo, activeElement was BODY
OBJECTIVE_CHECKS lists the console error '<svg> attribute height: Expected length, "auto"'

mimo.summary: A plain 2x2 grid of equal cards with a small side panel. Every plant's primary action says 'Watered', even for rotating, checking soil or misting, and the badges repeat themselves ('Today · Today'). Overdue care is not clearly prioritised, and focus is lost after actions.
strengths: No remote requests or errors; undo works; a queue pulse summary
weaknesses: The action labels don't match the tasks (Watered on all four)
A wall of equal cards; expanding one breaks the grid rows
Generic button names; focus goes to BODY after actions; 14 contrast failures
Minimal personality; no date context
evidence: Script: the done buttons for Orbit, Dot and Drama were all named 'Watered'
Desktop: the page is mostly empty below 600px; badges read 'Tomorrow · Tomorrow'

sonnet-5.5.summary: The boldest and oddest of the eight: sticker shapes with thick outlines, a brick-red overdue card, a little moss-creature mascot and bean-shaped marks for the weekly rhythm. Overdue care stands out right away, and every button names its plant. Two state bugs cost it points: it counts 3 plants after 4 are tended, and the detail panel still says '2 days overdue' next to 'Watered just now'.
strengths: Strongest overdue emphasis: a red OVERDUE section, then DUE TODAY, then a dashed UP NEXT
Button names are specific ('Mark Dot as soil checked', 'Snooze Drama until Thursday'); a modal dialog on mobile; focus moves to Undo and then back
Demo day is pinned to Sep 22 and the code comment explains why; relative ages are consistent
Rich detail view with light dots, a water timeline and observations
weaknesses: The all-done text says '3 plants looked after' even though 4 were tended
The desktop detail panel scrolls on its own and its history is cut off at the fold
Frida's wavy underline crowds the species line
evidence: Desktop screenshot: a three-column sticker layout; the right panel is clipped at 'Sep 16 Watered'
Script: Mark Frida as watered moved focus to 'Undo watered for Frida'; after undo, focus went back to the Mark button
After completing all four, the page read 'Everything's tended. 3 plants looked after.' and the panel still showed a '2 days overdue' pill
No contrast failures and no text under 12px in my audit

13-frontend-playful.notes: D and H are tied at 9.0; D is ranked first because it is more polished and has no state bugs, while H is bolder and odder (H counts 3 plants after 4 are tended and leaves a stale overdue pill in the detail panel). A is close behind. C, E and F show the real current date (Sep 30) against the fixed Sep 19–21 history; A takes only the weekday from the real clock.
